items.title: China posts weakest industrial profit growth this year, expanding 4.2% in August
items.body: Economists expect Beijing to lean harder on stimulus to stabilize corporate profitability, as consolidation accelerates in sectors facing sluggish demand and fierce competition.

items.title: Here's what happens to the economy when Treasury yields soar like they are now
items.body: Government debt costs leaped higher Wednesday, the product of multiple factors.

items.title: Surging Treasury yields pose a brand new problem for Kevin Warsh and the Fed
items.body: Markets expect the central bank will take a firmer hand on inflation. It's not that easy.

items.title: China saw 'surprise' jump in U.S. orders ahead of Trump-Xi summit, private survey shows
items.body: A private survey shows a rebound in China's exports to the U.S. as companies position for continued stability between the world's two largest economies.

items.title: Switzerland is keeping rates at 0% — for now
items.body: The Swiss National Bank held rates at 0% as low inflation and a strong franc enable it to diverge from other central banks, though markets expect hikes ahead.

items.title: Global debt tops $365 trillion as economists sound alarm over 'vicious cycle'
items.body: More is being paid out by advanced economies in debt interest than the whole world spends on AI, defense or clean technology.

items.title: France's fresh budget battle threatens to topple another government
items.body: Time is not on the side of French government bonds, strategists have warned, as the nation's deficit balloons.

items.title: World heads into food crises 'blind' as U.S. aid cuts squeeze UN food agency, experts warn
items.body: Climate shocks, conflict and a global fuel crisis, on top of surging interest rates and donor cuts, leave agencies less able to help those facing higher food prices.
